unpopular opinion: this is one of the best call of duty games.

here is why:

-advanced bots. the best bots in the series actually. the only ones to actually use their scorestreaks to my knowledge. 

-best "offline" play. although slightly botched compared to the console (you have to be connected to the internet), you can basically emulate 75% of the online experience "offline" with squads mode. in which you control and level up an entire team that learns as you play (allegedly).

-MW4. its MW4. It pays good respect to the universe if you enjoy it. 

-great sound, graphics, physics. the weapons feel great. there is even a hip fire only light machine gun. first game in the series to introduce hybrid optics.

you could go on for a while about the little bits of this game. I think it was really unnecessary how it was treated by critics and fans. It seemed to have by made with love for the most part. as long as youre at spec, which you probably are. the game runs fine. SSD is required though.

If you're a big fan of playing against bots, instead of competitively against other people, and you also enjoy playing other COD titles with bots then this game is nothing short of finding pure gold, IMO.

Forget the graphics (that was never where this game shined, and doesn't need to anyway)...it's the game play that makes this particular version in the franchise stand out above all others. First of all it has modes that you can play against bots that even in today's most recent versions you can not do, which is great.

But the very best thing about COD Ghosts is that you get to paly the "Unlock Weapons, Attachments and Leveling Up" meta all against the bots...you can level up to 60 and then do it again if you wish as a different character in your squad. As an option, there is also something called "SQUADS" mode that will create an automated playlist of the maps and as you play along from map to map it keeps changing the game mode as well automatically to keep the game play fresh and quite fun as you are leveling up...and it's all done against the bots!

People hated this game, mostly I think because gamers really don't want something new like this, as it means changing the way you're used to playing...and also because the bullet damage is severe and not forgiving..."time to kill" in this version of COD is lower than any other game in the franchise...it is near instant death if you get shot...maybe 2 shots but the guns shoot quite fast so it feels instant especially when playing either online against people or playing against the bots with them turned up.

Quite a few decent maps too. If you like bot-play and leveling up while unlocking stuff, and COD titles that are on the raw side (meaning they won't kiss yer arse) then this should be considered one of the best COD's in the franchise.

I only wish it wasn't so long in the tooth, being 9 years later now, I can't help but wish they'd do a new version of Ghosts and bring all this brilliant bot-play and game modes back to life with fresh graphics, sounds and lovingly hand-made maps.

This game, after release was woefully mis-judged because it might actually be the best one of the bunch...and truly deserves a comeback with a new refreshed version!

This is probably the most underrated Cod ever, and this might be a hot take, but I truly think that this is a top 3 Cod of all time. The only 2 I would put above this are MW3 and BO1. 

The Multiplayer for this game is not great and is probably the worst part due to the lack of good scorestreaks, somewhat underwhelming weapons, and the mediocre lethals and tacticals outside the sensor mine. Most of the maps are also pretty boring and lack good visuals and overall gameplay. All of that doesnt really matter since the servers for this game are dead, but it does bring this game down a bit for me.

Now onto the positives. Starting off, the campaign is solid, having a good and compelling story, good characters, gameplay, and a great ending. I personally think that its one of the best campaigns in any Cod game, and I would like to see a sequel to that story. 

Like MW3, this game also has a survival mode where you try to survive as long as possible. There is a 20 wave mode and also and endless mode. The only real problem I have with this gamemode is that you are again playing on the somewhat bad maps each having their own choke points.

What puts this above other Cods to me is the extinction gamemode. Most Cods, especially black ops have zombies, but Ghosts has extinction. This gamemode is like zombies, but instead of zombies, you are fighting an alien race, and instead of it being a round based gamemode, it is split up into 5 different missions where you have to complete different objectives while also surviving and eradicating the aliens.

There is a lot more to extinction, but that sums it up pretty well. Extinction is the main reason I still play the game to this day, and I would like to see a sequel to this game where they extend on the campaign story and extinction. 

As far as achievements go, they are very fun, with some being easy and some being hard. Most of them are tied to the extinction gamemode which makes them more worthwhile and fun. I've put hundreds of hours onto this game in the past years, but a new player will probably take longer than 100 hours of gameplay to get all the achievements, with me only taking 70-80ish hours of gameplay.

With that said, this game is great, and I would really like to see a sequel to it.

"Call of Duty: Ghosts" is a first-person shooter video game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision. Released in November 2013, it is the tenth main installment in the Call of Duty series. Here are some key details about the game:

Setting and Story
"Call of Duty: Ghosts" is set in a near-future scenario following a devastating event that reshapes the global balance of power. The storyline revolves around the "Ghosts," a group of elite U.S. special operations soldiers. Players primarily follow the journey of two brothers, Logan and Hesh, as they fight against the Federation, a powerful coalition of South American nations.

Gameplay
The game features the traditional Call of Duty elements, such as a mix of intense single-player campaigns and a variety of multiplayer modes. Some notable aspects include:

Single-player Campaign: The narrative-driven campaign features a blend of on-foot combat, vehicle sequences, and underwater missions.
Multiplayer: Introduces new game modes like "Cranked" and "Search and Rescue." It also features dynamic map events that can alter the battlefield during matches.
Squads Mode: Allows players to create a squad of soldiers with custom loadouts and AI behaviors to battle other players' squads online.
Extinction Mode: A cooperative game mode where players fight against alien creatures in a survival-style gameplay.
New Features
Character Customization: For the first time in the series, players can customize their character's appearance in multiplayer.
Dynamic Maps: Certain maps feature dynamic elements like collapsing structures and floods, adding a new layer of strategy.
Extinction Mode: A new cooperative mode where players fend off waves of alien creatures.
Reception
"Call of Duty: Ghosts" received mixed to positive reviews. Critics praised the game's multiplayer experience and the new Extinction mode, but the single-player campaign received mixed reactions for its story and lack of innovation compared to previous installments.

Technical Aspects
The game was released across multiple platforms, including PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Xbox 360, Xbox One, Wii U, and Microsoft Windows. It was one of the launch titles for the PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, showcasing the capabilities of the new hardware.

Legacy
Despite mixed reviews, "Call of Duty: Ghosts" was a commercial success, selling millions of copies worldwide. It contributed to the ongoing popularity of the Call of Duty franchise and introduced several features that influenced subsequent titles in the series.

Overall, "Call of Duty: Ghosts" stands out for its unique narrative, the introduction of new gameplay modes, and its role as a bridge between console generations.
